summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier proprietary models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with enterprise consumption increasingly flowing through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx. Open-weight models from DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen have captured significant developer mindshare on HuggingFace by delivering near-frontier performance at a fraction of the cost. Because the live research data contains many unverifiable or speculative version numbers, this ranking conservatively uses only model names that can be confirmed as currently available.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Consistently the highest-volume model by API calls and the default in most developer tooling, with massive enterprise reach through Azure OpenAI Service.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring multimodal input and reliable tooling.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Confirmed in research as shipped February 17, 2026 matching Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing; dominant in coding workflows and available via AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.
models.best_for: Software development, agentic coding, and enterprise automation.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Referenced in research as the 'Context Window King' and distributed at scale through Google Vertex AI, driving strong enterprise adoption.
strengths: Deep Google Cloud / Vertex AI integration
models.best_for: Long-document analysis and large-context enterprise workloads.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: High-volume, low-cost workhorse model widely adopted for high-throughput tasks and available natively on Vertex AI.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: Cited in research as a 671B MoE model and the cheapest frontier-class reasoning model; extremely popular on HuggingFace for open-weight deployment.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: Widely downloaded open-weight general-purpose MoE model offering near-frontier performance at very low cost, popular for self-hosting.
models.best_for: Affordable general-purpose and self-hosted LLM applications.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: One of the most downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and widely available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI for enterprise self-hosting.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Fast, low-cost member of the Claude family popular for high-volume agentic and classification tasks, available via AWS Bedrock and Vertex AI.
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive agentic and classification workloads.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Leading open-weight MoE model from Alibaba with rapidly growing HuggingFace adoption and strong multilingual performance.
models.best_for: Multilingual and open-weight deployments in Asia-Pacific markets.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading frontier model, widely adopted in the EU for data-sovereignty reasons and available through AWS Bedrock and Azure.
models.best_for: European enterprises requiring data sovereignty and multilingual support.
